title: Adoption Signal Bridge & Prelaunch Readiness Sheet
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines the 'Signal Bridge'—a compact mapping from telemetry & product KPIs to launch gates and rollback triggers. The goal is to make launch decisions (go / pause / abort / rollback) deterministic and measurable across adoption and infra signals. Use as the primary checklist during canary and 0→100% ramps.

1) Summary of approach
- Signal Bridge means: map each adoption metric and infra metric to: normal range, early-warning threshold, must-stop threshold, responsible owner, action playbook.
- Three gate phases: Canary (0.5–2% traffic), Ramp (2–25%), Broad (25–100%). Different thresholds per phase.
- Emphasis on both business signals (activation, retention, errors per MAU, conversion) and platform signals (P95 latency, token cost, error budget).

2) Key adoption KPIs (tracked daily + realtime dashboards)
- New user activation (day0 activation): baseline 12% → target +50% lift for launch to be declared successful. Canary threshold: >10% drop vs baseline for 6h triggers investigation. Must-stop: >25% drop vs baseline for 2h.
- Day 7 retention (cohort): baseline 18%. Ramp target: no regression >5pp. Must-stop if cohort retention drops >12pp across two cohorts.
- NPS signal (in-app microsurvey): Canary requires feedback panel to be enabled; early-warning if <0 (net negative) from pilot users.
- Feature conversion (opt-in CTA click→use): expected 8% conversion. Early-warning: drop below 5% for >24h.

3) Platform & reliability signals
- Request P95 latency: target < 300ms for median prompt length. Early-warning: sustained 400–500ms for 15min. Must-stop: >800ms or 50% increase vs baseline for 30min.
- Error rate (5xx + model timeouts): baseline <0.6%. Early-warning: >1% for 10min. Must-stop: >3% for 10min.
- Token cost per request (avg): expected $0.012. Early-warning: +40% MoM spike in rr cost. Must-stop: +100% sudden jump tied to routing or model mismatch.
- Rate limiting/falls-to-degraded model: track % routed to fallback. If >10% of requests use fallback for 1h, pause ramp.

4) Signal Bridge table (example rows - copy into dashboard):
- name | phase | metric | normal | early-warning | must-stop | owner | action
- new_user_activation | canary/ramp | day0 activation | 12% | -10% rel for 6h | -25% rel for 2h | product-analytics | investigate cohort, pause ramp if persists
- p95_latency | canary/ramp/broad | P95 latency ms | <300 | 400–500 for 15m | >800 for 30m | eng-sre | throttle, rollback model variant, route to stable region
- error_rate | all | 5xx+timeouts % | <0.6 | >1% for 10m | >3% for 10m | eng-sre | cut traffic, engage on-call, revert config
- retention_d7 | ramp/broad | cohort d7 % | 18% | -5 pp vs baseline | -12 pp across 2 cohorts | product-ops | pause expansion, ship hotfix or experiment

5) Prelaunch checklist (must-have before Canary) - check boxes for sign-off
- [ ] Instrumentation: event schema and ids documented for activation/usage/cts (owner: analytics)
- [ ] Dashboards: realtime Signal Bridge dashboard created and shared (owner: product-ops)
- [ ] Alerting: concrete paging rules for early-warning/must-stop (owner: eng-sre)
- [ ] Rollback artifacts: validated traffic split config and rollback PR template in repo (owner: release-eng)
- [ ] Legal/privacy: data retention & PII review complete for telemetry (owner: security-and-compliance)
- [ ] Support readiness: triage playbook & canned responses in Zendesk (owner: customer-success)
- [ ] Canary cohort defined: list of pilot accounts and selection criteria (owner: solutions-eng)

6) Canary run plan (example timeline)
- Hour 0: release to 0.5% (pilot accounts) — verify instrumentation and sampling
- Hours 1–6: monitor 5min windows for early-warning signals, collect qualitative feedback from pilot users
- Hour 6: increase to 1% if no early-warnings; otherwise investigate and pause
- Day 1: review curated KPI snapshot (activation, p95, error rate, cost). Decision poles: continue ramp / hold & mitigate / rollback

7) Rollout decision rubric (binary gates + primary evidence)
- Proceed rule: no must-stop triggers active + all early-warning items resolved within phase window + feature conversion within 90% of expected for pilot segment.
- Hold rule: any single early-warning not resolved within defined period (e.g., latency spikes >15min) or major user complaints from pilot cohort.
- Abort rule: any must-stop trigger fires, or data/PII concern raised by security.

8) Communication plan (who to ping when)
- Pager + Slack: eng-sre on-call @redwood/sre — immediate for must-stop
- Product thread: #product-prelaunch (product-ops lead) — every decision to be summarized in thread
- Exec escalation: if hold/abort extends >2 hours, trigger exec summary email (owner: head of product-ops)

9) Post-mortem & experiment loop
- If a hold or abort occurs: capture timeline, top 3 root causes, remediation plan, and a clear metric signal for reattempt.
- Required artifacts for reattempt: regression test PR, updated dashboard, stakeholder signoffs.

10) Quick reference: on-call run actions (condensed)
- Latency spike (P95 > 500ms): check autoscaling / queue length / model variant; scale pool + revert recent perf PRs if correlated.
- Error surge: capture sample error traces, rollback the most recent non-config change, cut traffic by 50% then iterate.
- Adoption drop: inspect cohort source, AB test allocation, check data processing pipeline for missing events.

11) Notes / open questions (editable)
- How to weight qualitative pilot feedback against small-n KPI volatility? (proposal: require both quantitative AND at least 3 independent qualitative signals to pause)
- Should we add cost-per-conversion as a live gate? (pro: aligns biz economics; con: noisy early)
- Confirm SLA/availability delta for early-access customers vs general availability.

12) Next steps (owners & due dates)
- Create Signal Bridge dashboard (owner: Alex Wu) — due 2024-10-20
- Finalize canary cohort list + consent notes (owner: solutions-eng) — due 2024-10-18
- Wire alerting into PagerDuty for must-stop flows (owner: Evan Li) — due 2024-10-22
- Draft customer communication templates for hold/rollback (owner: customer-success) — due 2024-10-21

Appendix: shortcuts & references
- Minimal dataset needed for dashboard: user_id, cohort_tag, event:activation, event:use, request_latency_ms, model_variant, error_code, cost_tokens_estimate
- Useful dashboards to clone: analytics/dashboard/adoption-signal-template, infra/dashboard/latency-shock
- Quick links: Confluence plan, JIRA PD-4821, rollout-configs PR #119

-- end working sheet --

(Notes: this is a working artifact intended to be iterated in the days before canary; copy into the permanent playbook after launch completes)
